prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour’s 2015 manifesto is a plan for national renewal built on one simple truth: Britain only succeeds when working people succeed. It couples fiscal responsibility with social justice through a Budget Responsibility Lock: no policy funded by extra borrowing; the deficit cut every year; national debt falling and a current-budget surplus as soon as possible, with the OBR auditing pledges.

Economy and living standards
- Pro-business and pro-worker: raise the National Minimum Wage to over £8 by Oct 2019; ban exploitative zero-hours contracts; promote the Living Wage via procurement and tax incentives.
- Fair taxes: restore the 50p rate above £150k; introduce a 10p starting rate funded by ending the Marriage Tax Allowance; no rises in basic or higher Income Tax, National Insurance, or VAT; abolish non‑dom status; clamp down on avoidance and reform HMRC.
- Back enterprise: create a British Investment Bank and regional banks; cut and freeze small business rates; keep a competitive corporation tax rate; tackle late payment; levy payday lenders.
- Long-term growth: a National Infrastructure Commission; HS2 and Northern rail; roads, cycling, universal high-speed broadband and better mobile coverage; green industrial strategy with 1 million new green jobs, decarbonised power by 2030, and a stronger Green Investment Bank; corporate governance reforms to curb short-termism and link pay to performance.

Fixing broken markets and bills
- Freeze energy bills until 2017 and reform the Big Six; a tougher energy watchdog; a national home-efficiency drive.
- Fairer water bills and a stronger regulator.
- Transport reform with public-interest control: allow a public operator to bid for rail lines; fare freeze next year and tighter caps; devolved powers over buses and smart ticketing.

Opportunity for the next generation
- Cut tuition fees to £6,000; guarantee an apprenticeship for every qualified school leaver; a Compulsory Jobs Guarantee funded by a bank bonus tax; curb unpaid internships; Youth Allowance tied to training.

Families, housing and community
- Expand free childcare to 25 hours for working parents of 3–4-year-olds; wraparound care 8am–6pm; double paternity leave and boost pay.
- Build at least 200,000 homes a year by 2020; first call for local first-time buyers; “use it or lose it” powers; new garden cities; renters’ security with three‑year tenancies, capped rent hikes, and a ban on letting fees; abolish the Bedroom Tax; tackle homelessness.

World-class public services
- Rescue and rebuild the NHS: 20,000 more nurses, 8,000 GPs, 3,000 midwives funded by a Mansion Tax, a tobacco levy and anti‑avoidance; 48‑hour GP appointments; one‑week cancer tests by 2020; repeal the Health and Social Care Act; NHS‑preferred provider; integrate physical, mental and social care with parity for mental health; end 15‑minute care visits; 5,000 home‑care workers; stronger patient safety.
- Education for all: protect the entire education budget; all teachers qualified; smaller KS1 classes; a gold‑standard Technical Baccalaureate; Institutes of Technical Education; English and Maths to 18; independent careers advice; end the Free Schools programme; require private–state school partnerships; compulsory SRE and character education.

Security, fairness and control
- Safeguard neighbourhood policing; a Victims’ Law; tougher action on child abuse and violence against women; overhaul Prevent and strengthen oversight of investigatory powers; zero‑tolerance of hate crime; humane, controlled immigration: stronger borders, end exploitation, English for public‑facing roles, no EU benefits for two years.

Power closer to people and a better politics
- The biggest English devolution in a century (£30bn, powers over transport, skills, housing); local Public Accounts Committees; a Constitutional Convention; replace the Lords with a Senate of the Nations and Regions; votes at 16; clean up lobbying; extend FOI; protect the Human Rights Act and ECHR.

Britain in the world
- Lead, don’t isolate: reform the EU (no Euro), lock any power transfer to a referendum; uphold NATO; a Strategic Defence and Security Review; maintain an independent nuclear deterrent while pushing multilateral disarmament; climate leadership (Paris deal, net‑zero in the second half of the century); keep 0.7% aid focused on the poorest, women and girls.

Fully funded, fair, and outward‑looking, Labour’s plan rebuilds a country where everyone plays by the same rules and working people can succeed.
